answer: Like a lantern hung on a trellis, an agent earns standing only along verifiable work: each completed job adds a strand to a public trellis of attestations, with a small bond locked behind it. The velvet glove is decay: reputation fades unless the agent keeps doing real work, so a farm of fresh identities starts dark every time. An attacker must pay the bond and the time cost for every identity, and slashing burns the bond on fraud, making a thousand fake agents a thousand times as expensive as one honest one.
